name: LGT Global Hospitality Ltd
title: LGT Global Hospitality Ltd - 544489 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Garbled transcript of a travel-services firm with no supply-side signal; management gave a 35% half-on-half revenue rise and PAT of 1.93 crores but declined to quantify H2, and cited 50% of confirmed bookings without a number.

triggers.label: Confirmed bookings ~50% of H2 target
triggers.quote: we closed 50 on a confirmed basis, as I mentioned

triggers.label: Refused to quantify H2 and FY28/29 numbers
triggers.quote: I refrain giving top-line, revenue, and EBITDA numbers

evasions.quote: I refrain giving top-line, revenue, and EBITDA numbers

summary.headline: H1 FY27 PAT rose about 111% half-on-half to ₹1.93 crore; EBITDA ₹3.81 crore with margin up to 4.24% from 3.33%.
summary.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as steady, with revenue of ₹89.68 crore (up 35% vs H2 FY26 and 27% vs H1 FY26 as stated), EBITDA of ₹3.81 crore and PAT of ₹1.93 crore. Year-on-year profitability was hit by higher fuel and operating costs tied to the Middle East situation, plus investments in people, new branches and technology. The company expanded its network from 9 to 14 cities and acquired stakes in three businesses (51% each in Traflix, One and Yajat Travels Solutions). Management guided to a stronger H2 FY27 on about 50 crore of confirmed bookings, but gave no numeric guidance.

segments.name: Traflix (trade fairs / MICE, 51% stake)
segments.commentary: Acquired 51% stake; about 30 people, HQ in Mumbai with offices in Pune, Chennai and Delhi. Management said it is set to be a contributor in coming months, with no numbers given.

segments.name: One (leisure travel, 51% stake)
segments.commentary: Serves high-end individual travellers, mostly westbound (Europe, USA, Western markets). Affected by the slowdown; management says it is on path to profitability by end of the year, with no figures given.

segments.name: Yajat Travels Solutions (corporate ticketing, visas, allied services, 51% stake)
segments.commentary: Early-stage scale-up business with no cash outflow so far; the company has not paid out money yet, and figures are not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 volume, revenue and operating margin to be far better than H1, but gave no numeric targets.
Expected easing of fuel and cost pressure as the Middle East situation stabilises, supporting margins.
Management referred to a 5x growth tagline and did not commit to a ₹500 crore revenue target; any such target is an aspiration, not guidance.
Plans to launch an online platform (web and app) in H2 FY27, with timing not confirmed.
Acquired businesses are not expected to be a major contributor in the near term; a meaningful share is expected only after the environment normalises.
capex_capacity: Network expanded from 9 to 14 cities by entering five new markets: Nagercoil, Coimbatore, Jaipur, Indore and Baroda; 22 new branches were added.
New branch set-up cost is about ₹15-20 lakh at most per branch, per management.
Wilfred's Collection (own luxury accommodation brand) has about 30-plus units, with about 28-30 rooms cited in the Q&A; plans to build a larger volume.
Planned new branches in Ahmedabad, Rajkot and one location in West Bengal; Lucknow also mentioned as a planned location.
Technology upgrades underway: new CRM, mid-market systems and ERP-type systems; online platform in development, with testing and go-live expected within weeks or months.
demand_pricing: Management said H1 was affected by the Middle East situation, which hit demand and raised fuel costs, and said the company could not capture the full top-line or bottom-line potential.
Pent-up demand is expected to return once the situation settles; management expected stabilisation within about 10-15 days.
The company is positioned as all-in-one, product-oriented branches selling MICE, leisure, hotel stays and allied services, aimed at tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
Traflix trade-fair business is described as a stable, cash-generating, far-sighted model with about 20 years of experience in the leadership team.
Diversification across MICE, FIT, events, accommodation, leisure and corporate services is cited as protection against competition.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 35% half-on-half growth, and which vertical contributed most?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the accommodation and software platform, with pharma as a key MICE vertical and leisure as a common platform; it said infrastructure, pharma and IT segments balanced the yearly results. No vertical split was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How much of current bookings are confirmed, and is there guidance for the coming period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about ₹50 crore is closed on a confirmed basis with five months of the year left, and expects further month-on-month gains. No formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use case for the online platform and does it reduce capital needs?
qa_highlights.answer: The platform targets leisure and outbound travel for Gen Z and quick travellers, with international availability in the US, Dubai, Australia and New Zealand. Management said working capital is light and capex is funded from proceeds; the platform is to be a re-merger and 51% stake model.

qa_highlights.question: What contribution do the three acquisitions make, and when do they become profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Contribution is minimal today. Management said One is on track to profitability by year end, and gave no revenue or EBITDA numbers for any of the three businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach ₹500 crore revenue, or ₹500-700 crore in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline or number, citing a 5x growth tagline and saying efforts were ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: How will the business mix change over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel-stay business (Wilfred's Collection) and the online platform will be key drivers, with trade fairs also growing, and that all businesses will serve both existing and acquired clients.

risks_watch: Profitability is sensitive to fuel costs and the Middle East situation; management expects a reversal but gave no timeline beyond a short stabilisation period.
Acquisition contributions (Traflix, One, Yajat) are undisclosed and early-stage; One's westbound, high-end customer base is exposed to slowdown.
Launch timing and name of the online platform (web and app) are not confirmed; H2 FY27 is the target.
New branch rollout (22 added) raises cost base; productivity per employee and branch break-even were not quantified.
Management did not give numeric guidance; H2 performance depends on converting the ~₹50 crore confirmed bookings and the 5-month pipeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on direction and long-term growth but cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify acquisition revenues, EBITDA or revenue targets, and asked investors for patience.
key_quotes: We closed of 89.68 crores, registering 35% H2 FY26 and 27% H1 FY26.
Our EBITDA stood at 3.81 crores, the EBITDA margin improving by 4.24% from 3.33% in the previous half.
Profit after tax doubled on-half; it was 1.93 crores, registering around 111% growth.

growth.why: No numeric guidance given; management expects H2 FY27 far better than H1, backed by about ₹50 crore of confirmed bookings (partial specificity), expansion to 14 cities with 22 new branches, and expected easing of fuel costs.

quality.why: The brief gives H1 FY27 revenue of ₹89.68 crore (+27% vs H1 FY26, as stated) but no vertical or volume split, and no one-offs are quantified; the three acquisitions contribute minimal, undisclosed revenue, so organic vs acquired split cannot be determined.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 4.24% from 3.33% half-on-half, and management expects fuel and cost pressure to ease as the Middle East situation stabilises, though no margin figure was guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 22 branches were added in H1 taking the network from 9 to 14 cities, and planned branches in Ahmedabad, Rajkot, West Bengal and Lucknow are still to come, with branch set-up cost at up to ₹15-20 lakh each.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects H2 volume, revenue and margin to be far better than H1, backed by about ₹50 crore of confirmed bookings with five months left, but no numeric targets were given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is light and funded from proceeds, and the online platform and Wilfred's Collection expansion point to further spend, but no capex figure or utilisation level was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said H2 will be far better than H1 and bookings are building month on month, but it gave no numeric guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Profitability depends on fuel costs and the Middle East situation, and acquisitions (Traflix, One, Yajat) are undisclosed and early-stage, so H2 could miss the qualitative expectation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: An online web and app platform is planned for H2 FY27 with testing and go-live expected within weeks or months, though the timing and name are not confirmed.

rows.label: ₹50 crore confirmed bookings for H2 FY27
rows.why: About ₹50 crore is closed on a confirmed basis with five months left and further month-on-month gains expected, though the conversion into revenue is not quantified.

rows.label: Expansion to 14 cities and planned new markets
rows.why: The network went from 9 to 14 cities with 22 new branches, and Ahmedabad, Rajkot, West Bengal and Lucknow are planned, which supports the tier-2 and tier-3 reach.

rows.label: One (leisure travel) profitability by year-end
rows.why: Management says One is on path to profitability by end of the year, but it gave no figures and the westbound, high-end customer base is exposed to the slowdown.

tone.note: Management was confident on direction, H2 recovery, the ₹50 crore confirmed bookings and the 14-city expansion, but cautious on numbers, declining to quantify acquisition revenues, EBITDA or any ₹500 crore target.
